messages:
jess (support): FYI customer (ACME) hit an issue where their CSV export downloads as a 0-byte file when they use our CLI with --compress and a large date range (>30d). They sent presigned link, preview shows headers-only in console. Repro steps below.

omar (eng): Thanks — quick q: is this only via the CLI or also from Console -> export?

jess (support): Only repro'd via CLI so far. Console web export works for them. CLI flow: `redwoodctl export download --job-id 4a1b2c --compress --out acme.csv` they see download complete but file size 0.

maya (analytics): Any chance the job succeeded server-side? Can you paste job JSON / status?

jess (support): Job status: `completed` in UI. Attached job meta snippet they pasted: `rows_estimate: 1_200_000, storage: s3, presigned_url: https://s3...&X-Amz-Signature=...`

liam (sre): I pulled the presigned URL and did a `curl -I` — got `HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content` and `Content-Length: 0`. That smells like a range/Content-Encoding mismatch between our upload and the client request (gzip + range).

omar (eng): Ugh we had a flaky path where we uploaded gzip bytes but included no content-encoding header on the presigned PUT, then the download path sends range requests expecting compressed chunks. Can you attach the exact CLI `--compress` behavior? Is the CLI requesting ranges?

jess (support): Customer says we return 200/complete when using `--no-compress`. Repro steps they provided:

```
# reproduce
redwoodctl export create --range 2025-01-01:2025-02-15 --format csv
redwoodctl export wait --job-id 4a1b2c
redwoodctl export download --job-id 4a1b2c --compress --out acme.csv
```

On their machine the file is 0 bytes. `curl -v` to the presigned URL shows repeated `206` with zero-length bodies.

maya (analytics): Could be our exporter switching to multipart upload + gzip and S3 returning 206 for range reads of compressed objects. Also I saw similar when clients (Win10 Excel) expect windows-1252 and choke on utf-8 BOMs, but that wouldn't produce 0 bytes.

omar (eng): Agreed. I'll instrument the export service to log `Content-Encoding` and multipart upload metadata. If we uploaded gzipped data but the presigned GET doesn't include `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, and the CLI performs ranged GETs, some ranges might map to offsets that are invalid for compressed stream -> 0-length chunks.

liam (sre): Temporary mitigation: advise customer to download with `--no-compress` or use `aws s3 cp "<presigned-url>" ./acme.csv` (full GET, avoid range). That worked in their testing.

jess (support): Sent the workaround to ACME. They can tolerate the slower download, but they'd like a permanent fix. Escalating to eng. Ticket: #SUP-12894.

omar (eng): I'll assign a PR to force full GETs on CLI when `--compress` is set (or include `Accept-Encoding: gzip` consistently and avoid ranged reads). Also adding server-side header `Content-Encoding: gzip` on uploads should help. Will run a quick canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: export-service/patch-ceramic -> canary on prod cluster (region us-west-2) in 10m.

jess (support): Thanks — I'll update the customer after canary. Also note: ACME reported Excel opens the no-compress CSV with weird characters; Maya, can we add a note about charset (UTF-8 vs windows-1252) in the export docs?

maya (analytics): Yep — will add a doc blurb and an optional `--charset` flag proposal for the CLI to force `windows-1252` transform. Will file a follow-up doc ticket.

omar (eng): Canaries green -> rolling out patch. I'll post results here in ~30m.

liam (sre): Monitoring and alerting added for `export:zero-byte-download` metric to catch regressions.

jess (support): Great, closing loop when PR merged. Thanks all :tada:
